What condition on γ ensures that a^nν converges to Haar measure λ on L/Λ as n→∞?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be a Lie group, $G \le L$ a closed subgroup, and $\Lambda \le L$ a lattice. Let $a \in G$ be a semisimple element, and let 
$$U = \{u \in G : a^{-n} u a^{n} \to e \text{ as } n \to +\infty\}$$
be its expanding horospherical subgroup in $G$. Fix a point $x_0 \in L/\Lambda$ such that the orbit $G x_0$ is dense in $L/\Lambda$. Let $\gamma : [0,1] \to U$ be a real-analytic curve, and let $\nu$ be the pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$ under the map $t \mapsto \gamma(t) x_0$. Let $\lambda$ denote the (normalized) Haar measure on $L/\Lambda$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the curve $\gamma$ under which the translated measures $a^n \nu$ converge in the weak-$*$ topology to $\lambda$ as $n \to \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: Shah established equidistribution for analytic curves not contained in any proper subgroup of $G^+$ in several settings, and the analyticity assumption has been weakened in subsequent work (e.g., by Shah–Yang and others). Recent works extend results to products of SO(n,1) factors and to non-analytic curves. The general question of giving necessary and sufficient conditions on $\gamma$ in arbitrary $L, G, a$ is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Equidistribution of expanding translates of smooth curves in homogeneous spaces
status_evidence.snippet: a(t)-translates of a non-degenerate real-analytic curve in a (U+)-orbit get equidistributed in X; analyticity weakened recently by Shah and P. Yang.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results known under non-degeneracy/non-containment-in-proper-subgroup conditions; analyticity hypothesis has been relaxed.

status_evidence.title: Equidistribution of expanding translates of curves and Dirichlet's theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Shah resolved equidistribution under the condition that the analytic curve is not contained in any proper subgroup of G+.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient condition known in many settings; full necessary-and-sufficient characterization remains open in general.
